correctness.rationale: For \(n=p^{2a}q\), multiplicativity gives \(\sigma^{**}(n)=AC(q+1)\) and \(d^{**}(n)=4a\), with \(A=(p^a-1)/(p-1)\) and \(C=p^{a+1}+1\). Coprimality yields \(AC\mid4aq\) and \(q+1\mid4ap^{2a}\). The proof exhausts \(q<p\) and \(p<q\); elementary inequalities reduce the latter to \(a\le4\), and each residual case is closed exactly. Direct substitution verifies \(45\).
